draft_scope.vendor_agnostic_engine: OPERATOR FRAMING 2026-07-22 (authoritative for all Pillar-A work): Handshake is a MODEL/VENDOR-AGNOSTIC engine. Models are called through CLI/terminal today ONLY because Anthropic subscription plans block economical direct API use; Handshake is the wrapper/engine AROUND the CLI. The wrapper - never the vendor harness - owns: sandboxing models, seeing/allowing/denying/STOPPING tool calls (SC MT-011 SessionToolGate), hooks (SC MT-012), cron/scheduling (SC MT-013), and exposing Handshake API/primitives to models as governed tools (SC MT-014). Claude and GPT are the first two engines dropped into the wrapper; open-source and other vendor models follow later. Vendor harness behaviors recorded in the research basis (Claude stream-json mechanics, Codex app-server, Anthropic workflow methodology) were RESEARCH INPUT, not the design target - the target is Handshake-owned capability that survives vendor swaps. No vendor names in operator-facing surfaces, schema ids, or policy vocabulary; vendor specifics live only in per-lane adapters and classification-table data. If direct API access becomes viable, a direct lane replaces the CLI lane without touching wrapper capabilities.

draft_scope.intent:
- What: ONE work packet, two pillars, everything built in Rust inside handshake_core / handshake_native.
- PILLAR A - AGENTIC HARNESS TAKEOVER (= DEXTERITY KERNEL EXTENSION; see naming_note_dexterity) (steer + roles + lifecycle + merge-back + ACP): upgrade Handshake's agent lanes from one-shot null-stdin CLI spawns (official_cli_bridge.rs AttachedStdioContract::null_stdin_piped_output, prompt passed once as argv) to LONG-LIVED STEERABLE AGENT SESSIONS so Handshake can run the same workflows Anthropic's and OpenAI's own harnesses already have built in: (1) persistent worker sessions with mid-run prompt injection/steering (Claude Code bidirectional stream-json over stdin/stdout; Codex app-server JSON-RPC turn/start + turn/steer + turn/interrupt; session resume); (2) HANDSHAKE ROLES - productized, streamlined successors of the .GOV/roles/* startup inject-prompts, injected at session start via the harness (append-system-prompt overlay / agent-definition layer), reusable by Handshake itself AND by future projects built by Handshake; (3) GOVERNED MODEL-TO-MODEL ORCHESTRATION - an orchestrator model can launch worker models (local or cloud) THROUGH Handshake (SwarmCoordinator remains the single sanctioned spawn path, exposed to models as a governed tool surface) and can steer those workers mid-run (straight model-to-model steering plane); (4) MT DISPATCH LIFECYCLE - Handshake launches the worker with role + micro-task contract injected, the worker executes in an isolated workspace (e.g. git worktree bound to a microVM via worktree_vm_registry), and when done signals Handshake mechanically MT_IMPLEMENTED / READY_FOR_VALIDATION (structured output + completion event, never polling), and Handshake then signals the orchestrator model; (5) WORKTREE MERGE-BACK - close the verified gap that source_control.rs has no merge/rebase/cherry-pick/patch-extraction: isolated worktree work must be mechanically mergeable back to the target branch through the product; (6) ACP DUTY TAKEOVER - implement Agent Client Protocol client support (official Rust crate agent-client-protocol) so Handshake can take over the repo-governance ACP-broker duty currently performed by .GOV/tools/handshake-acp-bridge, running the same repo-gov workflows natively in the near future.
- PILLAR B - NOTES ANNOTATIONS + PROFESSIONAL-IDE PARITY: (1) HUNK-STYLE DIFF/FILE ANNOTATIONS in the native Notes module - annotations on diff hunks and file regions authored BOTH by the operator AND by models; modeled on modem-dev/hunk's agent-annotation sidecar concept but with hardened anchoring (Gerrit-style path+side+line-range anchor PLUS Hypothesis-style redundant selectors: quoted snippet + context, fuzzy re-anchor via diff-match-patch-rs; explicit ORPHANED state on anchor failure, never silent mis-attach) and Gerrit-robot-comment-style machine provenance (robot_id/session_id/run_id + optional machine-applicable fix_suggestions). Annotations-for-models-in-files is a first-class cross-surface concept: Notes ships it first; the annotation core must be a reusable seam that Studio and Stage adopt in LATER work packets (rollout there is out of scope here); (2) REMOVE THE LEGACY TS/REACT NOTES EDITOR (app/src/lib/editor/, app/src/lib/tiptap/ Tiptap/ProseMirror surface) once native parity evidence is recorded, so no future work accidentally builds on it; (3) VS-CODE/ANTIGRAVITY PARITY GAP CLOSURE - the native notes/code editor is still missing many features required for a professional-grade IDE; produce a machine-readable parity gap matrix (VS Code + Antigravity feature baseline vs native editors, including the currently-DEFERRED native block-level prose diff in diff_engine.rs) and close or explicitly defer each gap.
- Why: Handshake will take over repo-governance ACP duty in the near future and must support the exact workflows the operator already runs through Claude Code/Codex harnesses (role injection at startup, per-MT steering, mechanical completion signaling). Straight model-to-model steering is required for the orchestrator-worker pattern. Model-facing file annotations are a foundational collaboration primitive for Notes, then Studio and Stage.

- An orchestrator model running in Handshake can launch a worker model (local AND cloud lanes) through the governed tool surface and steer it; parent-child attribution recorded; ungoverned direct spawn remains impossible.
- Full MT loop proven end-to-end: Handshake spawns worker in a VM-bound git worktree, worker signals MT_IMPLEMENTED / READY_FOR_VALIDATION mechanically (structured output + event, zero polling), Handshake notifies the orchestrator model, validation handoff fires.
- Worktree merge-back: work committed in an isolated session worktree is merged to the target branch through the product, with conflicts surfaced in the native merge UI; no force-push path exists.
- ACP: Handshake drives at least one real repo-gov-shaped session over ACP (agent-client-protocol crate) end-to-end, demonstrating it can assume the .GOV/tools/handshake-acp-bridge duty.
- Every steer/interrupt/role-injection/MT-signal/merge action emits FR events and ledger rows; worker final reports pass an injection-scan before orchestrator ingestion; HBR-INT-009 three-tier diagnostic wiring on all new behaviors.
- Notes annotations: operator can annotate a diff hunk in the native editor GUI; a model can create/read annotations via the tool surface with mandatory provenance; annotations survive a file edit via re-anchoring or degrade to explicit ORPHANED (never silently wrong); annotation core compiles as a reusable seam with no Notes-only coupling.
- Legacy TS/React notes editor fully removed; native editor is the only notes surface; build/tests green; removal gated on recorded parity evidence.
- IDE parity matrix exists as a machine-readable artifact; every row closed or DEFERRED-with-reason; the native block-level prose diff (currently DEFERRED in diff_engine.rs) is implemented and rendered in the notes editor.

draft_scope.risks_unknowns:
- stream-json/control-protocol contract is under-documented upstream and moves across CLI patch versions (message queueing behavior changed in v2.1.205; interrupt subtype reverse-engineered). Mitigate: feature-detect via system/init capabilities, tolerate unknown event types, pin tested CLI version ranges per adapter, CI contract tests against the live CLIs.
- ACP has NO mid-turn steer primitive (sequential prompt turns, cancel-then-reprompt only) - if ACP were the only layer, steering degrades. Mitigate: ACP is the abstraction, native stream-json/app-server adapters carry first-class steering.
- Windows specifics: Claude session lookup is cwd/worktree-scoped and ACP adapter resume had Windows path-encoding breakage; Handshake runs on Windows. Mitigate: pin worker cwd to the session worktree; integration-test resume on Windows.
- Model-to-model spawn is a privilege-escalation surface. Mitigate: SwarmCoordinator remains the ONLY spawn path; caps/ceilings/consent gates/claim leases enforced; every model-initiated spawn/steer is ledgered and attributable; injection-scan on inter-model messages.
- Removing the TS notes editor while WP-KERNEL-012 is ACTIVE and uses it as the parity reference. Mitigate: removal MTs hard-sequenced after WP-KERNEL-012 parity evidence is recorded; coordinate on the shared worktree/branch.
- Merge-back semantics vs CRDT workspace semantics (WP-KERNEL-002) must not be conflated: git merge for worktree code, CRDT for live shared documents. Refinement must draw this boundary explicitly.
- Fuzzy re-anchoring cost on large files / short generic snippets (documented Hypothesis failure mode). Mitigate: position-first anchor, bounded fuzzy search window.
- Single-WP breadth: MT count is UNCAPPED BY DESIGN (operator decision 2026-07-21; any earlier numeric mention like 200+ is arbitrary, not a target or cap) - every MT must be independently implementable by a no-context model, and coverage caps, if any, must be logged, never silent.
- Codex app-server WebSocket transport is experimental; use stdio JSONL.

draft_scope.research_basis:
- SOURCES CHECKED (2026-07-21, two web research passes; full dossiers in session record):
  - Steering/harness mechanics: code.claude.com CLI reference + headless + Agent SDK streaming docs (verified flags: --input-format stream-json, --output-format stream-json, --replay-user-messages, --session-id, -r/--resume, --fork-session, --append-system-prompt(-file), --agent/--agents, --json-schema, --bare, capabilities feature-detection incl. interrupt_receipt_v1; queued mid-run user messages since v2.1.205; SIGTERM/exit-143 supervisor semantics); anthropics/claude-code issues #24594 (stream-json under-documentation acknowledged) and #41665 + Roasbeef claude-agent-sdk-go cli-protocol.md (reverse-engineered control_request/interrupt); OpenAI Codex non-interactive + CLI reference (codex exec --json JSONL events, exec resume, --output-schema, sessions under ~/.codex/sessions) and codex app-server JSON-RPC guides (thread/start-resume-fork-rollback, turn/start, TURN/STEER, turn/interrupt, approval requests, stdio default / experimental WebSocket); agentclientprotocol.com (JSON-RPC over stdio, session/new-load-prompt-update-cancel, stop reasons, NO mid-turn steer, 40+ agents, official Rust crates agent-client-protocol + agent-client-protocol-schema, Claude adapter @agentclientprotocol/claude-agent-acp).
  - Methodology: Anthropic 'Building Effective Agents' (workflow taxonomy: prompt chaining, routing, parallelization, orchestrator-workers, evaluator-optimizer; simplicity-first) and 'How we built our multi-agent research system' (orchestrator + parallel subagents; every worker prompt carries objective / output format / tool guidance / task boundaries / effort budget; synchronous execution named as their own steering gap; durable resume + rainbow deployments; LLM-as-judge evals); Claude Code sub-agents + hooks docs (agent definitions as role layer, SubagentStart/Stop + TaskCompleted hook events, background completion notifications, injection-scan of subagent reports).
  - Annotations: github.com/modem-dev/hunk + hunk.dev (MIT, ~7.5k stars, active; agent-context sidecar JSON: changeset/file summaries + annotations {newRange, summary, rationale, author}; live-session comment targets hunk|hunkNumber|oldLine|newLine; NO drift handling; free-form author only); umputun/revdiff (explicit orphan-on-change policy); Gerrit CommentInfo/RobotCommentInfo (path+side+range anchor; robot_id/robot_run_id/properties/fix_suggestions; ported-comments re-anchoring); GitHub PR review comments API (line+side modern anchor; legacy diff-offset position deprecated; outdated-comment failure mode); reviewdog (filter modes for out-of-diff findings); Hypothesis fuzzy anchoring (multi-selector: position + quote + context, diff-match-patch Bitap fallback chain, perf caveat); git-notes (rejected: commit granularity, orphaning); VS Code Comment API (CommentController/CommentThread UI contract).
  - Rust reuse: similar (already in Cargo.toml, Myers), imara-diff, diffy-imara (unified-patch parse), diff-match-patch-rs / dissimilar (fuzzy re-anchor engine), mpatch; agent-client-protocol crate.
- SELECTED APPROACH: internal session model = Thread/Turn/Item with steer+interrupt (Codex app-server shape); transports = Claude stream-json bidirectional stdio first, Codex app-server JSON-RPC second, ACP crate as cross-agent abstraction; roles = append-overlay layer injected by harness at spawn; worker exit = structured output schema + hook-style completion events; annotations = hunk sidecar concept + Gerrit anchor/provenance + Hypothesis multi-selector re-anchoring on diff-match-patch-rs.
- REJECTED: codex proto (superseded); MCP as steering plane (poll-only, side-channel at best); one-shot -p --resume chaining as the steering story (the architecture being remediated); full --system-prompt replacement for roles (destroys agentic scaffolding); git notes as annotation storage; diff-offset anchors (deprecated field-wide); reusing hunk's TypeScript code directly (concept-only reuse); relying on undocumented control-protocol subtypes beyond interrupt.
- VALIDATION PLAN SEED: live runtime proof per lane (steer mid-run, interrupt, resume), end-to-end MT loop with zero polling, Windows-specific resume tests, CI contract tests pinned per CLI version range, annotation drift tests (edit-under-annotation, orphan determinism), removal build-green proof, parity-matrix completeness check.

assumptions_to_attack: A stub is planning metadata, not execution authority.
Model-to-model spawn/steer can bypass SwarmCoordinator governance (MUST be FALSE - single sanctioned spawn path, caps and consent gates always enforced).
Steering messages between models need no attribution or scan (FALSE - every inter-model message is ledgered, attributed, and injection-scanned before ingestion).
The stream-json contract is stable across CLI versions (FALSE - feature-detect capabilities, pin tested ranges, CI contract tests).
ACP alone can deliver mid-turn steering (FALSE - ACP is sequential; native adapters carry steering).
The TS notes editor can be deleted before native parity evidence exists (FALSE - removal is gated on recorded WP-KERNEL-012 parity evidence).
Annotations can silently re-attach to wrong lines after edits (FALSE - explicit ORPHANED degradation is mandatory).
Worktree merge-back may force-push or auto-resolve conflicts (FALSE - conflicts surface in the native merge UI; no force path).
A model author string is sufficient provenance for machine annotations (FALSE - robot/session/run identifiers are mandatory).
minimum_controls: Keep execution_authority=NON_EXECUTION_STUB until refinement + USER_SIGNATURE + official packet.
All model-initiated spawn/steer routes through SwarmCoordinator with existing caps, ceilings, leases, and consent gates; no new unsanctioned spawn path.
FR events + ledger rows for every steer, interrupt, role injection, MT signal, and merge action; fail-closed like existing lanes.
Injection-scan worker reports and inter-model messages before orchestrator ingestion.
CLI-contract integration tests pinned per adapter version range; capability feature-detection instead of version comparison.
TS-notes-editor removal MTs hard-sequenced after recorded parity evidence; build/tests must stay green through removal.
Annotation provenance mandatory for model authors; anchor-drift tests required; ORPHANED state explicit.
Merge-back never force-pushes; conflict resolution is operator-visible in the native merge UI.
MT coverage: no silent truncation - every planned gap row and lifecycle behavior gets an MT or an explicit DEFERRED verdict.
